title: Rational cohomology scalar comparisons respect coefficient towers
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$,
an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, a compactification $c_0$ of its structural morphism,
and $\epsilon\in\{\mathrm{ordinary},\mathrm{compact}\}$.
Use the canonical realization data of
[def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-realization-data].
Let $E\le L\le N$ be finite coefficient stages and $K\in C_E$.
Use the explicitly defined $H,q,c$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-comparison-factors], and the transition functors
$T$ and associator $a_{ELN}:T_{EL}\circ T_{LN}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{EN}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. In $D(N_{\rm sm})$ one has
$$
 F_{LN}(q_{EL,K});q_{LN,T_{EL}K};H_N(a_{ELN,K})
 =c_{ELN,H_EK};q_{EN,K}.
$$
Semicolons denote composition in diagram order. This equation is before the
final scalar-and-size extension into $D(\Omega)$.

source.place: (1.1.1)(d), canonical iterated coefficient extension, and (1.1.14), ordinary and compact cohomology; explicit factor of Steps 1--2 of the parent proof.

proof.text: Expand the integral operation scalar mates in the ordinary or retained compact-support recipe. Mate pasting and the normalized scalar units and counits identify the two-stage comparison with the direct comparison after the scalar associators. Restriction and total derived limit preserve this equality. Rationalize the identity; the component normalization defining frobeniusCohomologyRationalOperationScalar identifies the localized maps.

The normalized point-sections comparison has the corresponding scalar tower identity before size descent. Its finite-dimensional small comparison is uniquely fixed by that normalization; full faithfulness of the size lift detects the same tower identity. Whisker the operation identity with point fibre, compose with the point tower identity, and use naturality to interchange the intermediate operation and point comparisons.

Insert the inverse operationStageTransitionIso factors defining q. Their canonical comparison with the normalized stage-system transitions and associators changes the raw scalar tower into the displayed stage associator. Include the finite-dimensional target into D(N). This is precisely the displayed equation, also for equal fields and zero objects.
